question.problem:
Find, **in radians**, the **exact value** of the argument of $z=8\sqrt{3}-8\text{i}.$

**Hint**: The argument of a complex number is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$ 

$\operatorname{arg}⁡(z)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226152/assets/78399e67e0ba69c1d7848a41aa5d4a5f8040fc578aab30a99f7e19ac86ece179.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant of the complex plane. Hence $\frac{3\pi }{2}<\operatorname{arg}⁡(z)<2\pi .$ 

If $\alpha $ is the angle that $z$ makes with the positive real axis, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\alpha  & =\frac{8}{8\sqrt{3}} \\ \alpha  & =arctan\,(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z)=2\pi -\frac{\pi }{6}=\frac{11\pi }{6}.
$$
